sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File description and standard imports
sections.what: Describes the tool and its example commands. Loads standard Python tools for arguments, file paths, waiting, and time.
sections.why: Explains how to call the tool for anyone reading the file.

sections.name: load_env (part 1)
sections.title: Reading the API key from settings files
sections.what: Reads name and value lines from up to three possible settings files and adds only settings that are not already set.
sections.why: Keeps the API key out of the command line and the code.
sections.watch_out: A value already exported in the environment overrides the settings file, so an old exported key can be used without notice.

sections.name: load_env (part 2)
sections.title: Style and industry word lists
sections.what: Holds named style and industry phrases. Each chosen name adds its phrase to the logo request.
sections.why: Lets a short style name expand into detailed design instructions.
sections.watch_out: Phrases are used exactly as written, so small wording edits change the look of every future logo.

sections.name: enhance_prompt
sections.title: Building the full logo request
sections.what: Combines the base description with the brand name, style phrase, and industry phrase, then wraps the result in the logo instruction template.
sections.why: Gives the model consistent guidance for every logo it draws.
sections.watch_out: Unknown style or industry names are ignored silently, so the request may carry less detail than expected.

sections.name: generate_logo (part 1)
sections.title: Choosing model and setting up the request
sections.what: Checks for the API key, creates the client, builds the full request, selects the standard or pro model, chooses the aspect ratio, and prints a summary.
sections.why: Lets the user pick the quality tier and shape of the logo.
sections.watch_out: An unsupported aspect ratio quietly falls back to square with no warning.

sections.name: generate_logo (part 2)
sections.title: Sending the request and saving the image
sections.what: Sends the request asking for image and text back, with strict safety filters. Pulls the image data out of the reply and saves it as a PNG file.
sections.why: Turns the model reply into a logo file on disk.
sections.watch_out: Strict safety filters can block harmless brand names or words, which produces no image and no clear reason.

sections.name: generate_logo (part 3)
sections.title: Handling logo generation errors
sections.what: Catches any failure during the request, prints the message, and returns nothing.
sections.why: Keeps one failed logo from stopping a whole batch run.
sections.watch_out: Errors are turned into an empty result, so the caller must check for that or a failure looks like success.

sections.name: generate_batch (part 1)
sections.title: Preparing and generating style variants
sections.what: Lists nine preset styles with short descriptions, creates the output folder, and builds a request for each variant with a file name based on the brand and style.
sections.why: Gives a range of design directions to compare in one run.
sections.watch_out: The lettermark description hardcodes the letter U and the industry is always tech, so other brands get wrong guidance.

sections.name: generate_batch (part 2)
sections.title: Pausing between variants and reporting totals
sections.what: Reports which variants saved or failed, waits two seconds between requests, and prints a final total.
sections.why: The code says the pause is for rate limiting, so it spaces out requests to the service.
sections.watch_out: Failed variants are only printed, so the total can be lower than requested with no error exit code.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Command-line options and dispatch
sections.what: Defines all the options, handles the list options, requires a prompt or brand, and runs either batch or single generation.
sections.why: Gives users one command that covers every generation mode.
sections.watch_out: Batch mode without a brand name and without an output folder crashes, because the default folder name is built from the brand.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program start when run directly
sections.what: When this file is run as a program, it starts the main routine. When another file imports it, nothing starts.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern that lets other code reuse the functions here.

summary: Command-line tool that asks Google's Gemini image models to draw logo images for a brand and saves them as PNG files.
purpose: Creates logo candidates for a brand, either one at a time or as a batch of nine style variations to compare.
why: Likely reason: image models do the drawing, so no design software or designer is needed for first drafts.
how: Loads the API key. Builds a prompt from the brand name, chosen style, industry, and a logo template. Picks the standard or pro model. Asks for an image and text back. Extracts the image bytes and saves a PNG. Batch mode loops through nine preset styles with a pause between them.
inputs: A prompt, brand name, style, industry, output file or folder, batch count, extra brand context, the pro model flag, and aspect ratio.
outputs: PNG image files and progress messages on screen. The single-logo function returns a path or nothing. The batch function returns a list of saved paths, which the command line does not print.
risks: The brand name and prompt are sent to a Google service. Safety filters are set strict, so harmless content can be blocked and return no image. Batch mode always uses the tech industry and a letter U mark, which suits only one brand. Batch mode without a brand and without an output folder crashes. Failures do not set an error exit code.
debug: Confirm GEMINI_API_KEY is set and google-genai is installed. Read the message that says no image was generated. Try the standard model if the pro model fails. Check the output folder exists and is writable. For batch crashes, pass both a brand and an output folder.
